newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT - Aussie ready to get rate pain over with.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Aussie ready to get rate pain over with.

text.p: *AUD crept ahead offshore after finding good support beneath $0.7330, but capped by fresh offers atop $0.7380
*Market waits to see if RBA will deliver a long anticipated 50 basis point cut at its 9.30 am (2330 GMT) window
*Cut priced in so should not depress AUD too much, while silence would merely suggest delay until Aug 5 RBA board meeting

By 8.15 am (2215 GMT) the dollar was tensed at US$0.7361/66 having drifted to US$0.7387 offshore from US$0.7348/53 late here Thursday. Dealers were impressed by the extent of bids found beneath US$0.7330 yesterday when it suffered a knee-jerk dip in reaction to surprisingly low wage data.

Fresh offers had been met above US$0.7380 but dealers detected little sign of the hedge funds and New York investment houses which had led the selling assault on the A$ for the last four months. Where the dollar went from here depended largely on whether these powers decided to realise profits on their short positions or go for yet more on the downside.

The charts certainly held out the prospect of further losses with most long term indicators bearish and many analysts looking for a break of US$0.7305 to confirm a new phase of the downtrend to the 1995 low and Fibonacci target of US$0.7070/7100.
A push above US$0.7440 and crucially, US$0.7475, was needed to repair the technical position and the A$ would have to clear the US$0.7640/80 band to remove all downside risk.
If the RBA does not ease today, it will merely prolong the market's agony as attention would shift to the bank's monthly board meeting on August 5 in the expectation of a move the day after.

Assuming the bank does cut eventually, the dollar's fate would partly depend on whether the market viewed it as the last in the easing cycle. Most traders and analysts thought it was likely it would be, but emphasised a sixth move could not be ruled out if growth and unemployment continued to disappoint. That in turn suggested a sustained rally in the dollar could not be expected until unequivocal signs of an acceleration in economic growth came through.
Factors such as commodity prices also argued for caution, although the CRB index did bounce past key 236.00 resistance overnight to reach 237.74. -- Wayne Cole 61-2 9373 1800
